newsitem.title: UK: LME copper drifts lower, spreads narrow in dull LM.
newsitem.headline: LME copper drifts lower, spreads narrow in dull LM.

text.p: Copper drifted lower in sparse volumes on Friday during a low-key London Metal Exchange (LME) midday session, and the nearby backwardation narrowed slightly on profit-taking.
Three months copper received scant attention in the rings and ended the kerb $1 easier at $2,367 per tonne, after drifing down from pre-market highs above $2,380.
"There's been some profit taking, but we've barely seen any business in three-months copper," a senior trader said. "It's Friday and if anything things will come off a bit."
Support at $2,360 was expected to hold in the near term, but a fall below $2,350 would trigger stops, traders said.
Cash to threes backwardation iniitally flared further to $210, but later drew in to end up at $185/$195, which was some $15 narrower than on Thursday afternoon.
Tightness is mostly emerging from late April to early May, with the first tight date expected to be traded on Monday, traders said.
Cash for a day traded at $0.50 backwardation, while cash for two days was at $14. Meanwhile, April 30 to May 2 was quoted at $25/$30.
"We're not going to know what sort of squeeze this is until next week when we start trading these tight dates," a trader said.
Some profit taking was evident with one player lending 800 lots of May/threes copper at a $91 backwardation, traders noted.
The other metals generally followed copper's lead by paring any early gains and settling little different from Thursday's close.
Aluminium traded in a $7 range during the day, straddling the psychological $1,600 level. But like copper, it lacked the strength to hold onto its gains and wound up the kerb at $1,596, up just $2.

Zinc followed suit and shed the meagre gains of the morning, which had been generated despite a 2,775-tonne LME stock rise, and ended the kerb at $1,269, after trading as high as $1,279 in the pre-market.
Lead traded in a tiny range, ending $2 down at $634.
Nickel was unchanged at $7,450, while tin was $10 firmer at $5,730.
Alloy was indicated some $10 easier at $1,475/$1,480.
